pressure.title: Recovering caustic from carbonate
pressure.description: Carbon dioxide picked up by the liquor turns caustic into sodium carbonate, which does nothing useful. Adding slaked lime converts it back: Na₂CO₃ + Ca(OH)₂ → 2 NaOH + CaCO₃↓. The calcium carbonate solids are separated and the regenerated caustic returns to the circuit; conditions (temperature, liquor strength) are chosen to limit alumina losses as calcium aluminates.

foundation: Ring-wall or slab foundation designed for full liquid/slurry weight plus agitator dynamic loads; settlement monitoring for large tanks.
alignment: Tank plumb and level; agitator shaft vertical and concentric; check gearbox mounting.
piping: Nozzles sized for slurry velocity (avoid settling and erosion); flush connections; scaling-resistant design and descaling access.
Caustic service: suitable materials, gaskets and spray shields; eyewash/safety showers nearby.
commissioning: Water trials (agitator run with water, check vibration and power); then caustic/slurry; verify levels, interlocks and spillage containment (bunds).

lubrication: Agitator gearbox oil and motor bearings per maker; no lubrication for static parts.

safety: Lime is caustic and exothermic on slaking.

video_tutorials.title: Causticization Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Causticization Tank.
A causticization reactor regenerates caustic soda from sodium carbonate in the liquor by reaction with slaked lime: Na₂CO₃ + Ca(OH)₂ → 2 NaOH + CaCO₃.
The calcium carbonate is separated and the recovered caustic returns to the process.
Typical applications include caustic recovery in Bayer refineries; lime causticizing of green liquor in pulp mills.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Causticization Reactor: Agitator Shaft & Impeller, Slaker Paddle Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Causticization Tank — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Causticization Tank.
Check lime feed and agitator.
Descale reactor.
Slaker overhaul.
Watch for low efficiency: high carbonate. Common cause: poor lime quality, wrong conditions.
Watch for slaker blockage: lime build-up. Common cause: grit, low water.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
